title: The solar expo booth
intro: You walk up to a booth at a solar expo. Carlos works there. Start a conversation.

npc.es: Hola, bienvenido. ¿Es tu primera vez en este evento?
npc.en: Hello, welcome. Is this your first time at this event?

opts.es: Sí, es mi primera vez aquí
opts.en: Yes, it's my first time here
And you? Is it your first time?
Thanks, I like this event

steps.why: He asked if it's your first time; turning the question back or just being polite doesn't answer it.

npc.es: Mucho gusto. Me llamo Carlos. ¿Y tú?
npc.en: Nice to meet you. My name is Carlos. And you?

opts.es: Mucho gusto, Carlos. Me llamo Max
opts.en: Nice to meet you, Carlos. My name is Max
Carlos, nice to meet you. What's your name?

opts.es: Hasta luego, Carlos. Fue un gusto
opts.en: See you later, Carlos. It was a pleasure

steps.why: He gave his name and asked yours: greet him and say your name, don't ask his again or say goodbye already.

npc.en: What do you do for work?

opts.en: I work in solar energy
I live near this place
I'm very happy, thanks

steps.why: "¿A qué te dedicas?" asks about your job, not where you live or how you feel.

npc.en: How interesting! Do you have a business card?

opts.en: Yes, here's my card
I don't have a credit card
Thanks. Do you have a card?

steps.why: Hand over the card: "aquí tienes mi tarjeta". It's a business card, not a credit card, and he asked you.

title: Swap contacts
intro: The conversation with Laura went well. Time to stay in touch.

npc.es: Fue un gusto hablar contigo. ¿Nos conectamos en LinkedIn?
npc.en: It was a pleasure talking to you. Shall we connect on LinkedIn?

opts.en: Of course, with pleasure
Better not, thanks
Nice to meet you, Laura

steps.why: "Con gusto" is the friendly yes; the others refuse or greet her as if you had just met.

npc.en: Can you give me your number?

opts.es: Sí, claro. Aquí está mi número
opts.en: Yes, sure. Here's my number
Sure, can you give me your number?

opts.es: Lo siento, no tengo mi teléfono
opts.en: Sorry, I don't have my phone

steps.why: She asked for your number, so you give it; asking for hers or making an excuse doesn't answer.

npc.es: Te escribo esta semana. ¿Cuándo te viene bien?
npc.en: I'll write to you this week. When works for you?

opts.en: Thursday works for me
I did very well yesterday
And when are you free?

steps.why: She asked about timing, so name a day; talking about yesterday or asking her back gives no time.

npc.en: Perfect. Let's keep in touch.

opts.en: Of course. Thanks for your time
Thanks, but I don't have time
Perfect. See you tomorrow

steps.why: A warm close: thank her for her time; refusing or inventing plans for tomorrow doesn't fit "keep in touch".

title: Pitch a homeowner
intro: You knock on a door. Sr. Ramírez opens it. Use polite, formal Spanish.

npc.en: Good afternoon. How can I help you?

opts.es: Buenas tardes. Trabajo en energía solar. ¿Tiene un minuto?
opts.en: Good afternoon. I work in solar energy. Do you have a minute?

opts.es: Disculpe, señor, estoy muy perdido. ¿Me puede ayudar?
opts.en: Excuse me, sir, I'm very lost. Can you help me?

opts.es: Hola, buenas tardes. Vendo paneles solares. ¿Tienes un minuto?
opts.en: Hi, good afternoon. I sell solar panels. Do you have a minute?

steps.why: Introduce yourself and ask for a minute, politely; asking him for help flips the roles, and "tienes" is too casual.

npc.es: Mi recibo de luz es muy caro.
npc.en: My electricity bill is very expensive.

opts.es: Podemos reducir su recibo de luz con paneles solares
opts.en: We can lower your electricity bill with solar panels

opts.es: Entiendo, señor. Su recibo de luz es muy alto
opts.en: I understand, sir. Your electricity bill is very high

opts.es: Con paneles solares podemos reducir tu recibo de luz
opts.en: With solar panels we can reduce your electricity bill

steps.why: Connect his problem to your solution using "su"; agreeing offers no solution, and "tu" is too casual for Sr. Ramírez.

npc.en: How much does the installation cost?

opts.es: Hacemos una cotización gratis. ¿Me muestra su recibo?
opts.en: We do a free quote. Can you show me your bill?

opts.es: La instalación tarda solamente dos o tres días
opts.en: The installation takes only two or three days

opts.es: Señor, ¿usted me puede dar una cotización gratis hoy?
opts.en: Sir, can you give me a free quote today?

steps.why: He asked about the cost, so offer the free quote and ask for the bill; the others answer how long or ask him for a quote.

npc.en: Sounds good. When can you start?

opts.es: Podemos agendar una visita esta semana
opts.en: We can schedule a visit this week

opts.es: Ya agendamos la visita ayer, señor
opts.en: We already scheduled the visit yesterday, sir

opts.es: Qué bueno. Muchas gracias por su tiempo
opts.en: Great. Thank you very much for your time

steps.why: He asked when you can start, so propose a visit; "ayer" is the wrong time, and only thanking him doesn't answer.

title: "It's too expensive"
intro: Doña Elena likes solar but worries about the price. Stay formal.

npc.en: I don't know... it sounds very expensive.

opts.es: Se paga solo en pocos años
opts.en: It pays for itself in a few years
Yes, it's expensive, you're right

opts.es: No te preocupes, se paga solo
opts.en: Don't worry, it pays for itself

steps.why: Answer the objection with the payoff; agreeing gives up, and "no te preocupes" is too casual for a señora.

npc.en: And if I don't have money right now?

opts.en: We offer financing
We only accept cash
We have a full warranty

steps.why: Her problem is not having cash now, and only financing solves that; cash-only and a warranty do not.

npc.en: How long does the installation take?

opts.en: It takes two days
It costs two thousand
Thank you very much

steps.why: "Dura dos días" answers how long; the others give a price or only say thanks.

npc.en: Alright. Will you send me the quote?

opts.es: Se la mando hoy. Gracias por su tiempo
opts.en: I'll send it to you today. Thanks for your time

opts.es: Ayer se la mandé. Gracias por su tiempo
opts.en: I sent it to you yesterday. Thanks for your time

opts.es: Sale, al rato te mando la cotización
opts.en: Cool, I'll send you the quote later

steps.why: She asked you to send it, so say you will and stay formal with "su"; "ayer" is the wrong time and "sale" and "te" are too casual.

title: First coffee date
intro: A first coffee with Ana. Relax and be yourself.

npc.en: Hi, how are you?

opts.en: Very well, thanks. And you?
Fine, thanks. And you (formal)?
My name is Max. And you, Ana?

steps.why: Answer how you are and ask back with "¿Y tú?"; "usted" is too distant on a date, and your name answers a different question.

npc.en: What do you like to do?

opts.en: I like to travel and dance
I work in solar energy
I want a coffee with milk

steps.why: "Me gusta…" talks about what you enjoy; your job or your order answers other questions.

npc.en: Tell me about yourself. Where are you from?

opts.en: I'm from Slovakia
I'm thirty years old
You are from Slovakia

steps.why: "¿De dónde eres?" asks where you're from; your age answers another question, and "eres" talks about her, not you.

npc.es: Me la estoy pasando muy bien contigo.
npc.en: I'm having a really good time with you.

opts.es: Yo también. Me encanta tu forma de ser
opts.en: Me too. I love the way you are

opts.es: Qué bueno. Pero tengo que irme pronto
opts.en: Good. But I have to leave soon

opts.es: Gracias. Me encanta este lugar tan bonito
opts.en: Thanks. I love this very pretty place

steps.why: Return the warmth; saying you must leave or praising only the place ignores her.

title: The serious talk
intro: Second date. Ana wants to know what you're really looking for.

npc.en: What do you look for in a partner?

opts.en: I'm looking for something serious
You're looking for something serious
I'm very serious, Ana

steps.why: "Busco algo serio" says what you want in a partner; "buscas" is about her, and "soy serio" describes you instead.

npc.en: And what is important to you?

opts.es: La familia es muy importante para mí
opts.en: Family is very important to me

opts.es: Para ti la familia es muy importante
opts.en: For you, family is very important

opts.es: Mi familia vive muy lejos de aquí
opts.en: My family lives very far from here

steps.why: Share your own value: "para mí" is you, "para ti" is her, and where your family lives isn't what matters to you.

npc.en: I like that you're honest.

opts.es: Gracias, me gusta pasar tiempo contigo
opts.en: Thanks, I like spending time with you

opts.es: De nada, me gusta pasar tiempo contigo
opts.en: You're welcome, I like spending time with you

opts.es: Qué bonito. Me gusta mucho esta canción
opts.en: How nice. I like this song a lot

steps.why: Thank her and add something warm about her; "de nada" answers thanks she didn't give, and the song isn't what she said.

npc.es: ¿Nos vemos otra vez la próxima semana?
npc.en: Shall we see each other again next week?

opts.en: Of course. I'd love to
I loved it, thanks
Too bad, I'm busy

steps.why: "Me encantaría" is a lovely yes; "me encantó" is past tense, and being busy is a no.

title: Dinner for two
intro: You and your date arrive at a restaurant. The waiter greets you.

npc.en: Good evening. Table for how many people?

opts.en: Table for two, please
A table outside, please
Three people, please

steps.why: You and your date are two, so "para dos"; asking for a seat outside skips his question, and three is the wrong number.

npc.en: What would you like to drink?

opts.es: Una cerveza y un agua, por favor
opts.en: A beer and a water, please

opts.es: Un pollo con arroz, por favor
opts.en: A chicken with rice, please
We're very well, thanks. And you?

steps.why: He asks about drinks: order them; ordering food or answering a how-are-you doesn't answer.

npc.en: Anything else?

opts.es: No, gracias. La cuenta, por favor
opts.en: No, thanks. The bill, please

opts.es: No, gracias. La carta, por favor
opts.en: No, thanks. The menu, please
Thanks, good night. See you later

steps.why: Wrap up and ask for the bill: "carta" is the menu, and saying goodbye now means leaving without paying.

npc.en: That's five hundred pesos. Cash or card?

opts.en: By card, please
To go, please
Sorry, how much is it?

steps.why: He offered two choices: pick one; "para llevar" means to go, and asking the price again doesn't choose.

title: Lost in the city
intro: You can't find your hotel. A friendly stranger stops.

npc.en: Do you need help?

opts.en: Yes, I'm lost. Can you help me?

opts.es: No, gracias, sé dónde está el hotel
opts.en: No thanks, I know where the hotel is

opts.es: Sí, tú estás perdido. ¿Te puedo ayudar?
opts.en: Yes, you're lost. Can I help you?

steps.why: Say what the problem is: "estoy perdido"; saying you know the way contradicts it, and offering help flips the roles.

npc.en: Where are you going?

opts.en: I'm looking for the plaza
I'm coming from the plaza right now
I'm from Slovakia, Paloma

steps.why: "Estoy buscando…" names where you want to go; "vengo de" says where you come from, and your country answers another question.

npc.es: Está cerca. Todo recto y a la derecha.
npc.en: It's close. Straight ahead and to the right.

opts.en: Thanks. Is it far?
How much is the taxi?
Great. Was it far?

steps.why: A natural follow-up about distance: "¿Está lejos?"; a taxi price changes the subject, and "estaba" is the wrong tense.

npc.en: Five minutes walking.

opts.es: Muchas gracias. Que te vaya bien
opts.en: Thank you very much. All the best

opts.es: Buen provecho. Que te vaya muy bien
opts.en: Enjoy your meal. All the best

opts.es: Qué lejos. Mejor voy en taxi
opts.en: How far. I'd better take a taxi

steps.why: Thank her and say goodbye; "buen provecho" is for meals, and five minutes isn't far.
